comparisons.peer_topic: Definition and exclusions for FICO scores
comparisons.peer_summary: FICO scores measure borrower creditworthiness based on financial obligations and history; scores are refreshed quarterly or more frequently, but may not be updated for borrowers with debts discharged in bankruptcy.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs (GS) and Bank of America (BAC) utilize FICO scores as a primary metric to assess credit quality for consumer lending portfolios, specifically covering credit card and installment-like consumer loans. GS explicitly states that FICO scores are periodically refreshed to assess updated creditworthiness for installment and credit card loans. Similarly, BAC identifies FICO scores as a primary credit quality indicator for its Credit Card and Other Consumer portfolio segments, noting they are typically refreshed quarterly or more frequently to measure borrower creditworthiness based on financial obligations and history.

sentences.text: • For installment and credit card loans included in the other metrics/unrated category, the evaluation of credit quality incorporates the borrower's FICO credit score. FICO credit scores are periodically refreshed by the firm to assess the updated creditworthiness of the borrower. See "Vintage" below for information about installment and credit card loans by FICO credit scores.
FICO score measures the creditworthiness of the borrower based on the financial obligations of the borrower and the borrower's credit history.
FICO scores are also a primary credit quality indicator for the Credit Card and Other Consumer portfolio segment and the business card portfolio within U.S. small business commercial.

comparisons.peer_summary: Citigroup utilizes a risk management process to monitor principal risks in the consumer loan portfolio, actively tracking credit quality indicators such as delinquency status, FICO scores, and loan-to-value (LTV) ratios.
comparisons.comparison: Goldman Sachs and Citigroup both incorporate FICO scores into their credit quality monitoring frameworks for consumer loan portfolios. GS uses periodically refreshed borrower FICO credit scores to evaluate credit quality for installment and credit card loans. Citigroup similarly lists consumer credit scores under Fair Isaac Corporation (FICO) as an actively monitored credit quality indicator within its risk management process for the consumer loan portfolio.

comparisons.peer_topic: Role of credit scores in credit quality assessment
comparisons.peer_summary: While borrower credit scores provide a general indicator of credit quality trends, they are not viewed as primary indicators because they are lagging and do not capture all predictive factors; refreshed FICO score information for a random sample is provided as a secondary indicator.
comparisons.comparison: While both GS and JPMorgan use refreshed FICO scores to assess credit quality, they differ in the strategic weighting of this metric. GS incorporates refreshed FICO scores directly into the evaluation of credit quality for installment and credit card loans. In contrast, JPMorgan explicitly states that it does not view credit scores as a primary indicator of credit quality because they are lagging and do not capture all predictive factors; instead, refreshed FICO score information for a random sample is provided as a secondary indicator.

comparisons.peer_topic: Credit quality indicators for various loan types
comparisons.peer_summary: Credit quality indicators include internal risk ratings for corporate and commercial real estate loans, FICO scores and LTV ratios for residential real estate loans, and employment status for employee loans.
comparisons.comparison: Both firms use FICO scores as credit quality indicators, but for different loan segments. GS applies FICO scores to installment and credit card loans. Morgan Stanley applies Loan origination FICO credit scores specifically to residential real estate loans, alongside LTV ratios. Additionally, MS specifies that these scores are determined at origination by independent credit agencies, whereas GS emphasizes the periodic refreshing of scores for ongoing creditworthiness assessment.
